title: Introduce adaptive semantic palette and container-aware elevation system
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Our current token set has grown organically and exhibits visual inconsistencies in multi-component contexts: chart palettes feel disconnected from UI accent ramps, table row dividers clash with elevation steps, and dense components (compact tables, small buttons) use the same radius and shadow values as large container components, causing visual noise.

Goal: Create an adaptive semantic color palette (named tonal anchors) that maps to functional roles (bg-surface, bg-muted, accent-primary, accent-critical, success, info, neutral-ink) with light/dark variants tuned for both UI chrome and data viz. Introduce a container-aware elevation system that scales shadow/elevation micro-steps based on container scale (compact | default | expansive) so small controls keep subtle separation while large panels maintain depth. Update typography scale to reconcile dense layouts and dataviz label legibility, and refine spacing/radius tokens to support container-aware radii.

This ticket captures the design decisions, migration plan, and verification checklist for the tokens update.
acceptance_criteria: A semantic palette with 8 functional color roles and light/dark variants, with WCAG AA contrast for normal text against surface backgrounds
A container-aware elevation matrix with 3 scale classes (compact/default/expansive) and 5 elevation steps each, documented with shadow specs and token names
Updated typography scale with at least one condensed/compact variant for dense tables and chips, plus guidance for chart label sizes
Spacing and radius tokens that include container-aware radius variants (radius-compact/radius-default/radius-large), and migration notes for existing components
Design assets in Figma, a migration guide for engineers, and at least one component implementation PR for buttons and tables with visual diffs showing no regressions
Accessibility checklist passed: color contrast, focus ring visibility, motion reduced for elevation changes
tasks: Audit current tokens across components (buttons, inputs, tables, charts) and record deviations
Create semantic palette proposal with token names and sample mappings to existing swatches
Define elevation micro-ramp specs per container scale and generate CSS/variable examples
Propose typography tweaks for compact mode and update spec tokens
Prototype in Figma: components library update and chart palette variants
Write migration guide, deprecation table, and rollout plan
Coordinate with engineering to implement tokens in style-dictionary and runtime rollout in console and hosting docs
Open implementation PRs for tokens changes and component updates, run visual regression tests
decisions: Prefer semantic role names over numeric color ramps to reduce accidental misuse (e.g., use 'accent-primary' instead of 'blue-500')
Introduce container scale enums (compact/default/expansive) instead of per-component hacks to make elevation/radius predictable
Maintain separate chart-specific palettes derived from accent roles to preserve color-blind-safe variants without polluting core UI swatches
Adopt a 3-step deprecation window: warnings in lint + console during transition, then removal after two cycles
Keep absolute shadow offsets small for compact scale to avoid halo on small controls; emphasize inner separators for microseparation
notes: Initial audit completed 2026-02-10 by Aisha. Found 34 components using legacy numeric swatches and 12 components with hardcoded shadow styles. Early engineering spike (ENG-58421) validated that runtime variable swapping with feature flag will allow gradual rollout. Figma prototypes show compact buttons need radius reduced from 8px to 6px to maintain tappable area while reducing visual bulk.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Visual regressions in customer dashboards after palette swap. Mitigation: run canary rollout on internal tenant and create automated visual diff job across top 50 screens
Risk: Third-party charts using numeric colors will not adapt. Mitigation: provide mapping table and small script to translate old swatches to new semantic roles
Risk: Accessibility regressions due to palette changes. Mitigation: require contrast report artifacts and WCAG checks as part of PR checklist
reviews: Engineering implementation review in progress (Ethan Park)
